properties.desc: Asculum (modern Ascoli Piceno) was the principal city of the Piceni.

properties.name: Asisium
properties.desc: A Roman settlement built atop an earlier Umbrian one on a western foothill of the Apennines, Asisium received municipal status and was assigned to the Tribus Sergia. Totila destroyed most of the city in A.D. 545.

properties.name: Aternum
properties.desc: Aternum (modern Pescara) was a settlement at the mouth of the Aternus River.

properties.name: Attidium
properties.desc: An ancient settlement of Umbria mentioned only by Pliny the Elder. Numerous inscriptions discovered at the site indicate that Attidium achieved the status of a municipium.

properties.name: *Aufenginum
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 *Aufenginum

properties.name: Aufinum
properties.desc: Aufinum, long thought to have been located at modern Ofena, which reflects the ancient name, has been shown by recent excavations to have been located some 5km further south, near modern Capestrano. Aufinum was an ancient center of the…

properties.name: *Aurinia/Saturnia
properties.desc: *Aurinia/Saturnia was a settlement in Etruria. Dionysius of Halicarnassus claimed it was founded by the Pelasgians. Saturnia received a Roman colony in 183 BC.

properties.name: Auximum
properties.desc: Auximum (modern Osimo) is an ancient settlement of Picenum. The original foundation was likely carried out by Greeks from Ancona. The Romans made it a base for military operations from 174 B.C.

properties.name: Aveia
properties.desc: Aveia was a settlement of the Vestini in the valley of the Aterno River.

properties.name: Baccanae
properties.desc: Baccanae was a road station along the Via Cassia.

properties.name: Badies
properties.desc: Badies is a site (vicus) along the Via Salaria mentioned in the Antonine Itinerary. Its location is no longer certain.

properties.name: Balneum Regis
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C3 Balneum Regis

properties.name: Blera
properties.desc: Blera was a significant Etruscan settlement in the vicinity of Tarquinii. It lay along the line of the Roman Via Clodia. It received Roman municipal status and was enrolled in the tribus Arnensis. The city flourished in the sixth and fifth…

properties.name: Caelanum
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Caelanum

properties.name: Cales
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Cales

properties.name: Camerinum
properties.desc: Camerinum was a town in Umbria on the frontiers of Picenum that was allied to Rome from 309 B.C.

properties.name: Carsulae
properties.desc: An ancient settlement originating the late fourth or third centuries BC and lying along the route of the Roman Via Flaminia.

properties.name: Casone
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A2 Casone

properties.name: Castelluccio di Pienza
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Castelluccio di Pienza

properties.name: Castellum Firmanorum
properties.desc: Castellum Firmanorum was the ancient port of Firmum Picenum.

properties.name: Castelsecco
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Castelsecco

properties.name: Castro
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Castro

properties.name: Castrum Novum
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Castrum Novum

properties.name: Castrum Truentinum
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Castrum Truentinum

properties.name: Centum Cellae
properties.desc: Centum Cellae (modern Civitavecchia) was an ancient coastal settlement in Tyrrhenian Etruria. The emperor Trajan rebuilt the harbor at the site in 106/7 and Pliny the Younger mentions its name, Centum Cellae. Saracens destroyed the city in…

properties.name: Cetamura
properties.desc: Cetamura is an ancient hilltop settlement with occupation phases stretching from the Etruscans to the Romans to the Medieval period. The site is located near Gaiole, Radda and Castellina in Chianti, Italy.

properties.name: Chianciano Terme
properties.desc: Chianciano Terme begins as an Etruscan site, with a temple located near the natural springs. By the first century B.C. the site was popular with Romans as a healing spa.

properties.name: Cingulum
properties.desc: Cingulum was a town in Picenum.

properties.name: Civitalba
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D2 Civitalba

properties.name: Cliternia
properties.desc: A city of the Aequiculi located in the valley of the Salto river.

properties.name: Cluana
properties.desc: Cluana was an ancient settlement in Picenum.

properties.name: Colle Plinio
properties.desc: A hilltop villa near Tifernum Tiberinum commonly associated with one of the villas of Pliny the Younger.

properties.name: Collepezzuto
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Collepezzuto

properties.name: Contrada Altavilla
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Contrada Altavilla

properties.name: Contrada S. Rustico
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Contrada S. Rustico

properties.name: Cortona
properties.desc: An Umbrian city that, under Etruscan influence, expanded and came to be called 'Curtun'. Later it became the Roman colony of Cortino.

properties.name: Roman villa of Cortijo Robledo
properties.desc: A Roman villa rustica dated between the first and fifth centuries. The site occupies a low hill located to the south of Cerro de Robledo, near the Roman settlement of Aratispi. Archaeological fieldwork has demonstrated that the site was…

properties.name: Cupra Maritima
properties.desc: Cupra Maritima was a coastal city of Picenum (regio V) assigned to the tribus Velina.

properties.name: Cupra Montana
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Cupra Montana

properties.name: Cures
properties.desc: Cures (also Cures Sabini) was a Sabine city in the Tiber River valley along the Via Salaria. The Romans conquered Cures in 290 B.C. under M'. Curius Dentatus and granted it status as a municipium in the tribus Sergia.

properties.name: Eretum
properties.desc: Eretum was a settlement of the Sabines and is involved in legendary accounts of early Rome.

properties.name: Faesulae
properties.desc: Faesulae (modern Fiesole) was an Etruscan foundation called Viesul, Viśl, or Vipsul. The city was conquered by Romans in 283 B.C. Sulla would settle Roman veterans there. Citizens of the town supported the conspiracy of Catiline.

properties.name: Falerii
properties.desc: A fortified town located some 6 km from Falerii Veteres and established by the ancient Romans ca. 241 B.C.

properties.name: Falerio
properties.desc: Falerio was the site of a substantial ancient settlement on the left bank of the river Tinna. Under Augustus, a colony of veterans assigned to the tribus Velina was established there.

properties.name: Fanum Fortunae
properties.desc: Fanum Fortunae, the site of a shrine to Fortuna, is first mentioned in the ancient sources in 49 B.C. when Iulius Caesar held the town. An Augustan colony was established at the site and the Romans prevailed in the Battle of Fano in A.D.…

properties.name: Fanum Fugitivi
properties.desc: A road station on the Via Flaminia, located between Interamna and Spoletium.

properties.name: *Firmidianum
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 *Firmidianum

properties.name: Firmum Picenum
properties.desc: Firmum Picenum was founded as a Latin colony in 264 B.C. with 6,000 colonists. It received municipal status after 48 B.C.

properties.name: Fisternae
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Fisternae

properties.name: Fons Clitumni
properties.desc: Originally the site of a shrine dedicated to the river god Clitumnus and later a paleochristian shrine. The temple was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011.

properties.name: Fontecchio
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Fontecchio

properties.name: Foruli
properties.desc: Foruli was a Sabine town located between Amiternum and Interocrea.

properties.name: Forum Aurelii
properties.desc: A settlement in Etruria situated on the Via Aurelia between Centumcellae and Cosa according to the Antonine Itinerary.

properties.name: Forum Cassii
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Forum Cassii

properties.name: Forum Clodii
properties.desc: An ancient road station on the Via Clodia.

properties.name: Forum Decii
properties.desc: A town of the Sabines mentioned by Pliny the Elder.

properties.name: Forum Novum (Vescovio)
properties.desc: Forum Novum was a Roman town and an early medieval bishopric. It is located in the Sabine hills and was likely founded as a market center during the Republican period. It had achieved the status of municipium by the first century A.D. The…

properties.name: Forum Sempronii
properties.desc: An ancient Roman colony, founded in the time of Gaius Sempronius Gracchus.

properties.name: Fulginiae
properties.desc: Fulginiae was an ancient town of Umbria, Italy, on the later line of the Via Flaminia, ca. 20 km south of Nuceria.

properties.name: Galeata
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Galeata

properties.name: Grotte di S. Nicola
properties.desc: The so-called Grotte di S. Nicola, the remains of the platform and cryptoporticus of a late republican Roman villa.

properties.name: Grotte di Torri
properties.desc: Grotte di Torri is located on the left bank of the Tiber river in the modern comune of Montopoli di Sabina. It has been inhabited since pre-Roman times.

properties.name: Hatria (Picenum)
properties.desc: An ancient city of Picenum that may have originated as colony established by Etruscans from Adria in the Veneto region. An alternate narrative suggests that the city's origins may be as a late sixth century B.C. colony founded by Aegina.

properties.name: Heba
properties.desc: A Roman colony that was established in the third or second century B.C., Heba lay near modern Magliano. Funerary evidence indicates previous Etruscan occupation at the site.

properties.name: *Hercules Curinus
properties.desc: A sanctuary in the territory of the Paeligni dedicated to Hercules Curinus situated on an artificial terrace on the slopes of Mount Morrone. The terrace sanctuary looks over Sulmo in the valley below.

properties.name: Helvia Ricina
properties.desc: An ancient settlement in Picenum at modern Villa Potenza in Marche, Comune di Macerata, Italy.

properties.name: Helvillum
properties.desc: Helvillum was a vicus in Umbria located about 10 Roman miles from Aesis (Jesi).

properties.name: Hispellum
properties.desc: Hispellum (modern Spello) is an ancient settlement of Umbria that became a Roman colony in the first century BC.

properties.name: Histonium
properties.desc: Histonium, on the Adriatic coast, was a chief town of the Frentani.

properties.name: Horta
properties.desc: The Etruscan settlement of *Hurta (the modern Orte) was close to the Vadimonis Lacus where the Romans fought, and won, two engagements against Etruscan armies.

properties.name: Iguvium
properties.desc: An Umbrian hilltown, Iguvium is best known as the find-spot of the Iguvine Tables.

properties.name: *Incerulae
properties.desc: *Incerulae, an ancient sanctuary site in the territory of the Vestini.

properties.name: Interamna Nahars
properties.desc: An Umbrian center founded in the seventh century B.C. that became an important Roman municipality along the Via Flaminia.

properties.name: Interamnia Praetuttiorum
properties.desc: Originally a settlement of the Praetuttii located at the confluence of the rivers Tordino and Vezzola (modern Teramo).

properties.name: Intercisa/Petra Pertusa
properties.desc: Intercisa/Petra Pertusa was a road station on the Via Flaminia. The toponym derives from the rock-cut tunnel or galleria that dates to the reign of Vespasian.

properties.name: Interocrium
properties.desc: A Sabine town that was later known as a mansio on the course of the Via Salaria.

properties.name: Interpromium
properties.desc: A village of the Marrucini, forming a station on the Via Claudia Valeria between Corfinium and Teate.

properties.name: Lucus Feroniae
properties.desc: A sanctuary and grove of Feronia and an associated settlement located along the Via Tiberina in the territory of Capena.

properties.name: Lugnano
properties.desc: Lugnano in Teverina is a comune located in the Province of Terni in the modern Italian region of Umbria. It lies about 60 km south of Perugia and 25 km west of Terni. Archaeological investigation has documented important examples of villa…

properties.name: Marsiliana d’Albegna
properties.desc: An ancient settlement located near the confluence of the rivers Albegna and Elsa.

properties.name: Martanum
properties.desc: An ancient harbor of the city of Tarquinia.

properties.name: Maternum
properties.desc: Maternum was a settlement of ancient Etruria that is known from the Peutinger Table. It is located along the Via Clodia between Saturnia and Tuscana.

properties.name: Matilica
properties.desc: Matilica was a municipium in Umbria located near the source of the river Aesis and close to the borders of Picenum. The Liber Coloniarum identifies the settlement as one of the “Civitates Piceni.”

properties.name: Matrinum
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G3 Matrinum

properties.name: Mevania
properties.desc: Mevania (modern Bevagna) was a Roman municipium in Umbria located on the Via Flaminia. The town was enrolled in the tribus Aemilia.

properties.name: Mevaniola
properties.desc: Mevaniola was a Roman city located in the Bidente valley. Its inhabitants were of Umbrian extraction, connected with the settlement of Mevania (Bevagna).

properties.name: Mola di Monte Gelato
properties.desc: An ancient settlement 30 km north of Rome that was excavated from 1986-90. An imperial villa existed on the site up until the third century AD.

properties.name: Monte Calvo
properties.desc: The remains of a Roman villa that belonged to the family of the Bruttii Praesentes were found in the locality known as 'Madonna dei Colori' near the ancient road station Vicus Novus/Ad Novas, modern Osteria Nuova, some 53 km northeast of…

properties.name: Monteferetra
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Monteferetra

properties.name: Montefortino
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D2 Montefortino

properties.name: Nemora Vacunae
properties.desc: Shrine dedicated to a rural divinity of the Sabina.

properties.name: Nepet
properties.desc: Nepet had become a Roman town before 396 B.C. when Livy dubs it, along with Sutrium, as one of the "keys" to Etruria. It became a Roman colony in 383 B.C. and a municipium after the Social War.

properties.name: Nequinum/Narnia
properties.desc: Nequinum/Narnia (modern Narni) was an ancient settlement in Umbria. It became a Latin colony in 299 BC.

properties.name: Nuceria
properties.desc: Nuceria (modern Nocera Umbra) is an ancient town in Umbria, perhaps founded in the seventh century B.C. by Camerinum.

properties.name: Numana
properties.desc: Numana was a settlement of ancient Picenum located south of Ancona.

properties.name: Nursia
properties.desc: Nursia was the northernmost city of the Sabines.

properties.name: Ocriculum
properties.desc: An ancient Umbrian city that became allied with Rome in 308 B.C.

properties.name: Ortona
properties.desc: An ancient site in Italy that most likely originates with the Frentani.

properties.name: Ossaia
properties.desc: Site of a Late Republican and Imperial Roman villa (first to fifth centuries A.D.)

properties.name: Ostia Aterni
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G4 Ostia Aterni

properties.name: Ostra
properties.desc: Ostra was an ancient town of Umbria.

properties.name: Paganica
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Paganica

properties.name: Passo Corese
properties.desc: Passo Corese is located near Cures (Fara in Sabina). The site is often connected with Titus Tatius' march on Rome in 747 B.C.

properties.name: Perusia
properties.desc: A city of ancient Umbrian and Etruscan origin, Perusia aided Rome during the Second Punic War but was sieged and reduced by Octavian in the first century B.C. during campaigns against Lucius Antonius. It was rebuilt by Augustus and became…

properties.name: Solestà Roman bridge
properties.desc: A Roman bridge over the Truentus river.

properties.name: Porta Solestà
properties.desc: The Porta Solestà is one of the gates of Ascoli Piceno.

properties.name: Phalacrinae
properties.desc: A Roman town where the emperor Vespasian was born in A.D. 9.

properties.name: Pinna
properties.desc: Pinna (modern Penne) was a center of the Vestini. The site came under Roman control after the Social War (89 BC).

properties.name: Pisaurum
properties.desc: Pisaurum (modern Pésaro) was founded as a Roman colony in the territory of the Picentes in 184 BC.

properties.name: Pitinum
properties.desc: An ancient center of the Vestini.

properties.name: Pitinum Mergens
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Pitinum Mergens

properties.name: Pitinum Pisaurense
properties.desc: An ancient settlement in Umbria, known mostly via its inclusion in the texts of Pliny the Elder and Ptolemy, as well as by means of various epigraphic evidence.

properties.name: Planina
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Planina

properties.name: Plestia
properties.desc: Plestia was a municipium of the tribus Ufentina.

properties.name: Polimartium
properties.desc: An late Roman settlement associated with modern Bomarzo in Italy with nearby Etruscan antecedents.

properties.name: Ponte a Buriano
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Ponte a Buriano

properties.name: Ponte Capo d’Acqua
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Ponte Capo d’Acqua

properties.name: Potentia
properties.desc: A city settled in an area subjugated by Rome during the fourth century B.C. The local populace rebelled against Rome after the defeat at Cannae (216 B.C.), however the defeat of the Carthaginians eventually led to Potentia's…

properties.name: Punta La Penna
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 H4 Punta La Penna

properties.name: Quintianum
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Quintianum

properties.name: Raiano
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Raiano

properties.name: Rapinium
properties.desc: Rapinium is located on the coast of Etruria between Centumcellae and Graviscae, at modern Bagni Sant'Agostino.

properties.name: Reate
properties.desc: Reate (modern Rieti) was a major Sabine center that came to be captured by Manius Curius Dentatus in late third century B.C.

properties.name: Regis Villa/Regae
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Regis Villa/Regae

properties.name: Rostrata Villa
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Rostrata Villa

properties.name: Rusellae
properties.desc: An Etruscan city captured by Rome in 294 B.C., Rusellae's >2 mile circuit of megalithic walls represent an important early instance of stone fortification walling in the Italian peninsula.

properties.name: Sacraria
properties.desc: A station on the Via Flaminia near Le Vene.

properties.name: Saena
properties.desc: Saena was an Etruscan city that received a Roman colony (Saena Iulia) in the time of Augustus.

properties.name: S. Anatolia
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 S. Anatolia

properties.name: S. Casciano dei Bagni
properties.desc: The village of San Casciano dei Bagni, located south of Siena, Italy, has been frequented since at least the first millennium BCE on account of its thermal springs with supposedly healing properties.

properties.name: S. Pier Maggiore
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A1 S. Pier Maggiore

properties.name: S. Valentino
properties.desc: Remains of at least two Roman villas have been identified in the frazione of San Valentino, part of the larger comune of Poggio Mirteto. One is the so-called Villa dei Casoni, while this site is sometimes known as the Bagni di Lucilla.…

properties.name: S. Vittore
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 S. Vittore

properties.name: Sarsina
properties.desc: Sarsina was a town of the Umbri that was captured by Cornelius Scipio in 271 B.C. and was the birthplace of the Latin author Plautus. The necropolis at Sarsina has been extensively studied.

properties.name: Sarteano
properties.desc: Sarteano is located between the Val d'Orcia and the Valdichiana. It is known in particular for its rich evidence of Etruscan funerary culture.

properties.name: Sena Gallica
properties.desc: Senonian Gauls founded Sena Gallica at the mouth of the Misa River in the fourth century B.C. This place became the site of Rome's earliest colony on the Adriatic seaboard before 280 B.C. Pompeius Magnus destroyed the city in 82 B.C.

properties.name: Sentinum
properties.desc: An ancient town in the region of Italy now known as Le Marche, Sentinum is perhaps best known for the pivotal Battle of Sentinum of the Third Samnite War that took place nearby in 295 BC.

properties.name: Septempeda
properties.desc: Septempeda was an ancient settlement of Picenum. Its Roman phase began as a conciliabulum in the third century B.C.

properties.name: Sestinum
properties.desc: Sestinum was an ancient place in Umbria near the headwaters of the river Pisaurus. Pliny mentions the site, and its ancient name is preserved in modern toponymy.

properties.name: Settefinestre
properties.desc: A Late Republican Roman slave-run villa owned by the senatorial family of the Volusii.

properties.name: Sorano
properties.desc: Sorano was a Villanovan and, later, Etruscan settlement.

properties.name: Sorrina
properties.desc: Sorrina was a small Etruscan settlement on Viterbo's Colle di San Lorenzo, of which some traces remain. Epigraphic evidence also attests to a Roman municipium - Surrina Nova - that was likely located between Viterbo and Lake Bullicame.

properties.name: Spoletium
properties.desc: An ancient city along the route of the Via Flaminia; an initial colony was established there in 241 BCE.

properties.name: Piammiano
properties.desc: Site of an ancient settlement that flourished between the seventh century BCE and the early sixth century CE, located west across the Tiber from the modern village of Attigliano in Italy. Piammiano is probably to be identified with…

properties.name: Statulae
properties.desc: Statulae is a station marked on the Peutinger map. It was located in the territory of the Paeligni, 7 miles from Corfinium.

properties.name: Suana
properties.desc: Suana (Sovana) has Etruscan origins but later became a Roman municipium. In the fifth century A.D. it became an episcopal see.

properties.name: Suasa
properties.desc: Suasa was the site of a Roman municipium in Umbria. It lies in the Piano Volpello along a road from Cales to Sena Gallica. Alaric razed the settlement in 409.

properties.name: Succosa
properties.desc: Succosa was located between the Portus Cosanus and the Via Aurelia Antica to the north. It is mentioned in the Itineraries and located on the Tabula Peutingeriana. Frank E. Brown suggests that Succosa, derived from "sub-Cosa", emerges in…

properties.name: Superaequum
properties.desc: One of three towns of the Paeligni which possessed municipal rights.

properties.name: Sutrium
properties.desc: An ancient settlement along the line of what would become the Roman Via Cassia and described by Livy, together with Nepet, as one of the keys to Etruria. A Latin colony was founded at the site after the fall of Veii.

properties.name: Tadinae
properties.desc: Tadinae (Sant'Antonio della Rasina to the west of Gualdo Tadino) is an ancient municipium of Umbria and was a road station on the Via Flaminia.

properties.name: Talamone
properties.desc: Located along the road from Talamone to Cannelle are the archaeological remains of one of the largest maritime villas known in the Albegna valley. Referred to colloquially as Villa le Terme at Santa Francesca di Talamone, the remains of…

properties.name: Tifernum Mataurense
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Tifernum Mataurense

properties.name: Tolentinum
properties.desc: Tolentinum was a town of Picenum that is listed as having municipal status in the Liber Coloniarum.

properties.name: Traianus?
properties.desc: A Roman villa that is typically associated with the emperor Trajan.

properties.name: Trea
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Trea

properties.name: Trebula Mutuesca
properties.desc: Trebula Mutuesca or Trebula Mutusca was one of two Sabine cities bearing the name Trebula.

properties.name: Tuder
properties.desc: Tuder, modern Todi, is an ancient city of Umbria. Its foundation likely occurred during the eighth/seventh centuries BC, although legendary traditions associate the site with the activities of Herakles.

properties.name: Tuficum
properties.desc: Tuficum was an ancient city of Umbria located on the Aesis River. It became a municipium of the tribus Oufentina.

properties.name: Tuscana
properties.desc: An ancient city that traced its legendary origins to Ascanius, son of Aeneas. The site became an important Etruscan mercantile center and eventually achieved Roman municipal status in 88 B.C.

properties.name: Urbs Salvia
properties.desc: An ancient city of Regio V (Picenum) where a Roman colony was founded in the second century B.C.

properties.name: Urvinum Hortense
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Urvinum Hortense

properties.name: Vacchereccia
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Vacchereccia

properties.name: Velzna/*Volsinii Veteres/Urbiventus
properties.desc: Volsinii Veteres was one of the most powerful and important cities of Etruria, as it was the location of the important federal sanctuary located at the Fanum Voltumnae.

properties.name: Verucchio
properties.desc: Around the modern Italian town of Verucchio (Emilia-Romagna), a number of ancient necropoleis provide evidence for iron-age civilization and craft at a presumed settlement on the site lasting into the Roman period.

properties.name: Vespasiae
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Vespasiae

properties.name: Vettona
properties.desc: Vettona (modern Bettona) is an ancient settlement of Umbria located between Perusia and Mevania. Pliny the Elder lists it among the municipalities of Umbria, and it also numbered as one of the “xv Populi Umbriae".

properties.name: Vicarello
properties.desc: A large, Roman imperial estate covering ca. 2,000 ha on the shores of Lake Bracciano. The name may derive from Vicus Aurelius, suggesting a connection with Marcus Aurelius.

properties.name: Vicus Martis
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Vicus Martis

properties.name: Vicus Matrini
properties.desc: Vicus Matrini was a mansio along the Via Cassia, located between Sutri and Forum Cassi. The site's name is attested on the Peutinger Table.

properties.name: Vicus Novus/Ad Novas
properties.desc: Vicus Novus/Ad Novas

properties.name: Vignanello
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Vignanello

properties.name: Villa S. Silvestro
properties.desc: The remains of a Republican temple podium now support a Christian church at Villa S. Silvestro in Umbria. The temple's podium likely dates, in its first phase, to the third century B.C.

properties.name: Visentium
properties.desc: Visentium (Bisenzio) was an Etruscan settlement located on the shores of Lago di Bolsena. The site has yielded especially important evidence for Iron Age and Etruscan period burials.

properties.name: Volsinii
properties.desc: Volsinii, also referred to as Volsinii Novi, is thought to be the settlement where Rome resettled the survivors of the Volsinian rebellion of 264 BCE. This episode is discussed by Zonaras (8. 7. 8). A late republican center at Bolsena…

properties.name: Volusii
properties.desc: A villa associated with the Volusii Saturnini built ca. 50 B.C.

properties.name: Vulci
properties.desc: Vulci (originally Velch or Velx in Etruscan) was an Etruscan city 80 km northwest of Rome. Vulci was one of the duodecim populi Etruriae.

properties.name: Roman aqueduct at Arretium
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 unnamed aqueduct (Arretium)

properties.name: Triumphal Arch of Orange
properties.desc: A triumphal arch most likely built during the reign of Augustus to honor veterans of the Gallic Wars and Legio II Augusta.

properties.desc: Calatia was an ancient city of Campania located along the Via Appia between Capua and Beneventum.

properties.name: Cales (Campania)
properties.desc: Cales was an ancient city of Campania of Ausonian origins. The Romans captured the town in 335 B.C. and established a colony there.

properties.name: Campochiaro
properties.desc: An Italic sanctuary sacred to Hercules located in località Civitella in the comune of Campochiaro. The site is to be connected with the Pentrian Samnites.

properties.name: Villa Maritima di Capo di Sorrento
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Capo di Sorrento

properties.name: Capreae
properties.desc: Settlement on the island of Capreae.

properties.name: Capreae (island)
properties.desc: An island of the Bay of Naples off the Sorrentine Peninsula that has, since the time of the Roman Republic, been a popular seaside resort area. The emperor Tiberius maintained twelve villas on the island.

properties.name: Capriati
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Capriati

properties.name: Capua
properties.desc: An important ancient city of Campania with Villanovan and Etruscan origins.

properties.name: Carsioli
properties.desc: An ancient settlement along the Via Valeria, Carsioli was established as a Latin colony in the territory of the Aequi ca. 298 BC.

properties.name: Cascano
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Cascano

properties.name: Casilinum
properties.desc: A settlement located in the border region between the ager Falernus and the ager Campanus, north of Capua.

properties.name: Casinum
properties.desc: A Volscian hilltop settlement that became a Roman colony in 312 B.C.

properties.name: Castropignano
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Castropignano

properties.name: Castrum Novum
properties.desc: Castrum Novum was a colonia maritima established on the coast of Etruria.

properties.name: Caudium
properties.desc: A city of Samnium located between Capua and Beneventum. In 321 B.C., the Samnites under C. Pontius encamped there before defeating the Romans at the Battle of the Caudine Forks.

properties.name: Cereatae Marianae
properties.desc: Cereatae Marianae, purported to have been the birthplace of Caius Marius, is thought to have been located where the 13th-century abbey church of Casamari now stands (in the modern province of Frosinone, Lazio, Italy).

properties.name: Circeii 2
properties.desc: A port on the Tyrrhenian coast. In myth, the site was considered to be one of the stopping points of the hero Odysseus.

properties.name: Cliternia
properties.desc: A city of northern Apulia.

properties.name: Clostra (Romana)
properties.desc: Clostra (Romana) was a place in Latium along the Via Severiana. It was located 15 miles from Circei and 9 miles from Astura.

properties.name: Cluturnum
properties.desc: Cluturnum was a site in Samnium, located near Aesernia. Its exact location cannot be determined.

properties.name: Cocullo
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Cocullo

properties.name: Cumae/Kyme (Campanian)
properties.desc: An ancient settlement of Campania, Cumae was the first Greek colony established on the Italian mainland in the eighth century BC.

properties.name: Damecuta
properties.desc: An Imperial villa excavated by A. Maiuri in the 1930s, Damecuta was connected to the Iulio-Claudian emperors. The construction of later Medieval and Bourbon fortifications on the site significantly damaged the ancient remains. The Medieval…

properties.name: Diana Tifatina (temple)
properties.desc: The Fanum Dianae Tifatinae located on the slopes of Mt. Tifata in Campania.

properties.name: Dikaiarcheia/Puteoli
properties.desc: A maritime city of Campania situated on the Phlegrean Peninsula. The settlement started as a Greek colony and became a Roman colony under the name Puteoli in 194 B.C.

properties.name: Fabrateria Nova
properties.desc: Caius Gracchus dispatched a Roman colony to Fabrateria Nova in 124 B.C. The relationship between Fabrateria Nova and the earlier Volscian site of Fabrateria Vetus remains unclear. The favored location for Fabrateria Nova is at S. Giovanni…

properties.name: Fabrateria Vetus
properties.desc: Fabrateria Vetus was a Volscian settlement that surrendered to Rome in 424 B.C.

properties.name: Fagifulae
properties.desc: Fagifulae was a center of the Pentrian Samnites.

properties.name: Faustianum?
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Faustianum?

properties.name: Ferentinum
properties.desc: A Hernican town along the Via Latina that the Romans captured in 364 B.C. Later in the Republican period (after 195 B.C.), the city received Roman municipal status.

properties.name: Fonte Romito
properties.desc: A pre-Roman and Roman settlement of Samnium.

properties.name: Formiae
properties.desc: An ancient settlement of likely Greek origin along the Via Appia. Cicero was assassinated near Formiae (now Formia) in 43 B.C.

properties.name: Forum Popillii
properties.desc: An important town of the Ager Falernus, not to be confused with Forum Popili, the modern Polla.

properties.name: Fregellanum
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Fregellanum

properties.name: Frusino
properties.desc: Frusino (modern Frosinone) was a town in Latium along the Via Latina that was originally a Volscian settlement.

properties.name: Fundi
properties.desc: Fundi achieved civitas sine suffragio after the Latin War in 338 B.C.

properties.name: Gianola
properties.desc: The site of a villa associated with Lucius Vitruvius Mamurra.

properties.name: Gioia dei Marsi
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Gioia dei Marsi

properties.name: Giurlanda
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Giurlanda

properties.name: Grottacce
properties.desc: At Grottacce are the remains of a Roman seaside villa or villa maritima.

properties.name: Herculaneum
properties.desc: An ancient Roman town of Campania destroyed by the eruption of Mt. Vesuvius in A.D. 79. Named as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

properties.name: ‘Herculis Rani’?
properties.desc: A large fanum sacred to ‘Herculis Rani’? at Campochiaro, the name of which is then preserved in the station mentioned on the Peutinger Table. Scholars like Adriano La Regina support linking this fanum to a place mentioned by Livy, although…

properties.name: Interamna Lirenas
properties.desc: A Latin colony founded ca. 312 B.C. along the Via Latina. The site was sacked by Samnites (ca. 294 B.C.) and subsequently by Hannibal (212 B.C.). It received Roman municipal status in 90 B.C.

properties.name: ‘Invinias’
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 ‘Invinias’

properties.name: ‘Iovis Lareni’
properties.desc: ‘Iovis Lareni’ is marked as a station on the Peutinger map. It lies 7 miles from Sulmo. This place coincides with the ancient site of Ocriticum, a pre-Roman and Roman settlement. The site, located in the Italian comune of Cansano (province…

properties.name: Iuvanum
properties.desc: A Roman municipium founded in 87 BC after the Social War, Iuvanum sits on the site of a pre-existing Samnite settlement that occupies an upland plateau.

properties.name: Kupelternum/Cubulteria
properties.desc: Kupelternum/Cubulteria was an ancient Samnite settlement.

properties.name: Lago di Paola
properties.desc: A villa of the emperor Domitian located in the area of Circeii.

properties.name: *Lavernae
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 *Lavernae

properties.name: Ligures Baebiani
properties.desc: Ligures Baebiani was a Ligurian settlement in Samnium.

properties.name: Liternum
properties.desc: An ancient city of Campania located near the mouth of the Volturnus River; a Roman colony was established at Liternum in 194 B.C. The site is most famous as the location of the villa of Scipio Africanus, as described by Seneca.

properties.name: Lucus Feroniae
properties.desc: A sanctuary of Feronia located at a spring on the via Appia near Tarracina.

properties.name: Malborghetto
properties.desc: The hamlet of Malborghetto, located on the ancient Via Flaminia, is traditionally linked with Constantine the Great and his visions of victory that occurred prior to the battle of Saxa Rubra on 28 October A.D. 312. The quadrifons arch…

properties.name: Marica
properties.desc: Marica, an Italic goddess, was worshipped in a sacred grove located between Minturnae and the estuary of the Liris river.

properties.name: Marruvium
properties.desc: Ancient Marruvium was the principal city of the Italic tribe of the Marsi.

properties.name: Matrice
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Matrice

properties.name: Mignano
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Mignano

properties.name: Minerva temple at Punta della Campanella
properties.desc: An ancient temple of Minerva, located on the ancient cape that also was known by the goddess' name.

properties.name: Minori
properties.desc: Minori is the site of a major villa located on the Amalfi coast, some 11 km WSW of Salerno. Destroyed by a possible landslide, the villa was in use from the Iulio-Claudian period through to the Flavian period.

properties.name: Minturnae
properties.desc: Originally an Ausonian town that fought against Rome in 314 B.C., Minturnae became a colony in 296 B.C. The site is located on the Garigliano river (ancient Liris) and served an important economic function. The Via Appia passes through the…

properties.name: Misenum
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Misenum

properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Monte S. Croce

properties.name: Monte Saraceno di Cercemaggiore
properties.desc: Archaeological excavations on the area of the summit of Monte Saraceno have documented the remains of an imposing, fortified high-altitude settlement which has a second walled area within it.

properties.name: Mura di S. Stefano
properties.desc: A second century A.D. Roman villa built atop an earlier villa rustica.

properties.name: Neratii
properties.desc: This site of an imperial villa, dating to the first and second centuries, covers an area of ca. 15,000 sq. m. It is located in the southern portion of the modern civic territory of San Giuliano del Sannio in the Província de Campobasso…

properties.name: Nola
properties.desc: The city of Nola (Nuvlana) is considered one of the oldest in Campania. Under Augustus, the settlement became a Roman colony; it was the spot where Augustus died in A.D. 14.

properties.name: Nuceria (Alfaterna)
properties.desc: Nuceria (Alfaterna) (modern Nocera Inferiore) is an ancient settlement in Campania. In pre-Roman times, this was the chief settlement of the Sarnus river valley.

properties.name: *Nuceriola
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G3 *Nuceriola

properties.name: Oplontis
properties.desc: An ancient place (modern Torre Annunziata in Italy), lying between Pompeii and Herculaneum and buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 CE. Its ancient name is known only from Peutinger's Roman Map.

properties.name: Pagus Capriculanus?

properties.name: Pagus Vescinus
properties.desc: The Pagus Vescinus is only attested epigraphically.

properties.name: Palazzo a Mare
properties.desc: The site of one of the twelve villas of Tiberius, and perhaps the largest, on the island of Capreae.

properties.name: Parthenope/Neapolis
properties.desc: Founded as Parthenope by Greeks in the eighth century B.C., the site eventually gave rise to Neapolis in the sixth century B.C. and was one of the most prominent cities of Magna Graecia. Present-day Naples, Italy.

properties.name: Pitonia?
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D2 Pitonia?

properties.name: Pompeii
properties.desc: An ancient city of Campania destroyed by the volcanic eruption of Mt. Vesuvius in A.D. 79, Pompeii was named as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

properties.name: Pons Apollinis

properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Pons Campanus

properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Pons Tirenus

properties.name: Privernum
properties.desc: A Volscian center that Rome reportedly destroyed in the late fourth century B.C.

properties.name: Punta Eolo
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D4 Punta Eolo

properties.name: Pyrgi
properties.desc: Pyrgi is an ancient Etruscan port city on the Tyrrhenian coast of Italy. A Roman colony was established at the site by 191 B.C. In 1964, the bilingual 'Pyrgi Plaques' were discovered during the course of excavations.

properties.name: Rufrae
properties.desc: A Samnite settlement at the margins of Campania.

properties.name: Saepinum
properties.desc: An ancient town of Samnium captured by the Romans in 293 B.C., located on the road between Beneventum and Corfinium.

properties.name: Salernum
properties.desc: A city of Campania with Osco-Etruscan origins that became a Roman colony in 197 B.C.

properties.name: S. Giacomo
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 S. Giacomo

properties.name: S. Rocco
properties.desc: The San Rocco villa was built during the second quarter of the first century B.C. It was initially a simple villa rustica and it was later enlarged substantially.

properties.name: S. Vincenzo al Volturno
properties.desc: S. Vincenzo al Volturno is a multi-period settlement. In pre-Roman times, a phase of Samnite occupation has been identified. By the fifth century A.D., the site was occupied by a large agricultural estate (villa) that was abandoned in the…

properties.name: Saticula
properties.desc: Saticula was a Samnite site in Campania that received a Latin colony in 313 B.C.

properties.name: Sava di Baronissi
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Sava di Baronissi

properties.desc: An ancient city of Latium located in the valley of the Liris River that likely had Volscian origins. The Romans captured the city in 345 BCE and later established a colony there in 303 BCE after the Second Samnite War.

properties.name: Speluncae
properties.desc: An ancient grotto, associated with the nearby Villa Tiberii, at the modern Italian town of Sperlonga.

properties.name: Stabiae
properties.desc: An Oscan and Roman settlement located on the bay of Naples.

properties.name: Suessa Aurunca
properties.desc: The ancient center of the Aurunci, Suessa Aurunca was abandoned in 337 B.C. for a more favorable site (modern Sessa) where a Latin colony was established in 313 B.C.

properties.name: Suessula
properties.desc: Suessula was an important ancient city of Campania.

properties.name: Sulmo
properties.desc: A chief settlement of the Peligni that was ravaged by the Carthaginians during the Second Punic War.

properties.name: Super *Tamari Fluvium
properties.desc: Super *Tamari Fluvium is the name of a station (statio) mentioned by the Antonine Itinerary.

properties.name: *Supinum
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 *Supinum

properties.name: Surrentum
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Surrentum

properties.name: Tarracina(e)/Anxur
properties.desc: A strategic Volscian city that had come under Roman control by 509 B.C.; a Roman citizen colony was established there in 329 B.C. The site is particularly notable for the remains of the terraced sanctuary of Iuppiter Anxur.

properties.name: Teanum Sidicinum
properties.desc: Teanum Sidicinum (modern Teano) was the capital of the Oscan-speaking Sidicini tribe. The city likely submitted to Rome after 334 B.C.

properties.name: Telesia
properties.desc: An ancient Samnite city located in the valley of the Calor River.

properties.name: Terventum
properties.desc: Terventum was the site of a Roman municipium established in the territory of the Pentrian Samnites.

properties.name: Terzigno

properties.name: Torre S. Limato

properties.name: Treba
properties.desc: Treba (modern Trevi nel Lazio) was originally a settlement of the Aequi.

properties.name: Trebula Balli(ni)ensium
properties.desc: An ancient city of Campania that became enfranchised in the Roman system in the late fourth century B.C.

properties.name: Treppete
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Treppete

properties.name: Uscosium?
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Uscosium?

properties.desc: A sanctuary of the Pentrian Samnites on the flanks of Monte Capraro, north of the modern Italian village of Vastogirardi.

properties.name: Venafrum
properties.desc: Venafrum was an ancient town of Campania.

properties.name: Verulae
properties.desc: Verulae is an ancient city that became a Roman municipium in 90 B.C. Modern Veroli in Italy.

properties.desc: A preserved gate of the Roman city wall in the district Mainz-Kästrich.

properties.name: Ponte Latrone
properties.desc: A Roman bridge on the Volturno river located near Capriati.

properties.name: Ponte Romano di Val d'Assano
properties.desc: An ancient bridge located to the east of ancient Teanum Sidicinum (modern Teano in Italy).

properties.name: Sacra Via
properties.desc: The Sacra Via (Sacred Way) is one of Rome's oldest urban streets and its main sacred route, extending from the top of the Velia (summa Sacra Via) to the Forum Romanum.

properties.name: Ulrichsberg
properties.desc: The ruins of a Late Gothic Church of St. Ulrich which gave its name to the mountain on which it stands.

properties.name: Temple of Divus Augustus (Rome)
properties.desc: Caius dedicated a temple to divus Augustus in Rome in the autumn of 37 CE. Based on the sources, the temple should be located between the vicus Tuscus and the vicus Iugarius, just behind the Basilica Iulia. The temple remains unexcavated…

properties.name: Roman theater at Cádiz
properties.desc: The Roman theater at Cádiz was one of the largest in the Roman world, accommodating some 20,000 spectators. It dates originally to the first century B.C. In the thirteenth century it was incorporated into a fortress built by King Alfonso X…

properties.name: Ara della Regina
properties.desc: A fourth to third century B.C. sanctuary at Tarquinia.

properties.name: Roman baths at Vertillum
properties.desc: The remains of baths at the Gallo-Roman site of Vertillum.

properties.name: Roman amphitheater at Volaterrae
properties.desc: The archaeological remains of an amphitheater were discovered at Volterra in 2015. Preliminary work suggests that the structure measured ca. 70 x 90 meters and had three tiers of seats that could accommodate 8,000 to 10,000 spectators.

properties.name: House of the cithara player
properties.desc: The so-called "House of the cithara player" (I,4,5 and 25) opens both on to the Via Stabiana and the Via dell'Abbondanza. One of the largest aristocratic homes in Pompeii, it was formed from two adjoining properties.

properties.name: Urso theater
properties.desc: The Roman theater of Urso.

properties.name: Roman amphitheater at Richborough
properties.desc: The earthwork remains of the Roman amphitheater associated with the Saxon Shore fort at Richborough.

properties.name: Los Villares (Huétor-Tájar)
properties.desc: Los Villares (Huétor-Tájar) is an archaeological site located in the community of Los Villares (Huétor-Tájar). Here remains of a significant settlement dating to the third to sixth centuries CE have been discovered.

properties.name: Roman city wall of Zaragoza
properties.desc: The Roman city wall of Zaragoza was begun under Tiberius, although work continued through the third century. The wall once stretched some 3,000 meters and had 120 defensive towers.

properties.name: Arch of Augustus at Aosta
properties.desc: The Arch of Augustus at Aosta is a commemorative arch dedicated to Augustus ca. 25 BC following victories over the Salassi.

properties.name: Arles Amphitheatre
properties.desc: The Arles Roman amphitheater or Arènes d'Arles was built ca. A.D. 90 and could seat over 20,000 spectators.

properties.name: Roman forum at Tergeste
properties.desc: The Roman forum of Tergeste.

properties.name: Castrum Invi
properties.desc: An Italic site located at the mouth of the Incastro river and in the territory of Ardea.

properties.name: Harpole Roman villa
properties.desc: A Roman villa north of Panattoni Park and adjacent to Junction 16 of the M1 motorway, excavated in the 1840s and in 1966.

properties.name: Pont Romà
properties.desc: A Roman bridge on the island of Majorca (Pollença, Mallorca, Spain).

properties.name: So-called Temple of Hercules
properties.desc: A site on the Via Appia that is likely commercial in nature but that has long been associated with a shrine mentioned by Martial.

properties.name: Lion gate of Butrint
properties.desc: The so-called "Lion gate" of Butrint is a fifth century A.D. gateway that reuses an Archaic Greek sculpted relief.

properties.name: Temple de Diane
properties.desc: The so-called "Temple de Diane" is a first century Roman monument on the Gard river dedicated to Augustus.

properties.name: Tour Magne
properties.desc: Situated atop Mount Cavalier, the so-called "Tour Magne" is a tower on the fortified walls of ancient Nemausus. The tower dates to the time of Augustus.

properties.name: Arènes de Cimiez
properties.desc: A Roman amphitheater of the second century that was enlarged during the course of the third, the so-called Arènes de Cimiez measures 67 by 56 meters.

properties.name: Altheim-Wagham villa rustica

properties.name: Scoglietto

properties.name: Pausilipum
properties.desc: Pausilipum was an ancient Graeco-Roman settlement on the Bay of Naples.

properties.name: Aphrodision at Akrai

properties.desc: A Roman timber amphitheater dating from the first to fifth centuries, the Künzing Roman amphitheater measured 46 by 40 meters. The site was discovered during excavations carried out in 2003 and 2004. The archaeological site is no longer…

properties.name: Roman theater of Acinipo
properties.desc: The Roman theater of Acinipo dates ca. 59-53 B.C.

properties.name: Mausoleum Campo Barbarico
properties.desc: The Campo Barbarico Mausoleum is a third-century CE Roman "temple tomb" located at the fourth mile of the Via Latina. The tomb's position is immediately to the south of the archaeological area of the Tombs of the Via Latina. In 2022…

properties.name: Via Triumphalis necropolis
properties.desc: A segment of an imperial necropolis preserved along a portion of a consular road on the Vatican Hill. The Via Triumphalis necropolis was uncovered during the construction of a parking structure in the Via del Pellegrino.

properties.name: Acharnai (N)
properties.desc: Acharnai (N) was the largest deme of ancient Attika, the sole inland deme of the tribe Oineis.

properties.name: Agrai
properties.desc: Agrai was a district of ancient Athens located south of the Ilissos River. Pausanias describes the temple of Artemis Agrotera as being located there. It was also the site of the Lesser Mysteries of Eleusis.

properties.name: Aigilia?

properties.name: Aigina (settlement)
properties.desc: The primary ancient settlement on the Aegean island of the same name.

properties.name: Aithalidai/Hybadai?
properties.desc: Aithalidai/Hybadai? was a deme of ancient Attica. Following the Cleisthenic reforms, Aethalidae was assigned to the phyle of Leontis. After 307/6 BCE, it belonged to the phyle of Antigonis. The deme's location is uncertain.

properties.name: Aixone
properties.desc: Aixone was an ancient coastal deme of the phyle Kekropis, located on the west coast of Attica south of Athens in the area of modern Glyphada.

properties.name: Alopeke
properties.desc: Alopeke was the only city deme of the tribe Antiochis in Attica

properties.name: Amarynthos
properties.desc: An ancient coastal settlement on the island of Euboea, located at modern Palaiokhoria/Kato Vathia (just east of the modern Amarynthos).

properties.name: Amphitrope?
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 D4 Amphitrope?

properties.name: Anagyrous
properties.desc: Anagyrous was a deme of ancient Attica.

properties.name: Anakaia?
properties.desc: Anakaia (or Anacaea) was a deme of ancient Attica and a part of the phyle of Hippothontis. It is thought to have been located near modern Mygdaleza.

properties.name: Angele
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 C3 Angele

properties.name: Ankyle Hypenerthen
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 C3 Ankyle Hypenerthen

properties.name: Ankyle Kathyperthen
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 C3 Ankyle Kathyperthen

properties.name: Temple of Aphaia on Aegina
properties.desc: An ancient sanctuary on the island of Aegina, dedicated to the autochthonous deity Aphaia.

properties.name: Aphrodite sanctuary at Dafni
properties.desc: An ancient sanctuary of the goddess Aphrodite, described by Pausanias and located at modern Dafni (Daphne) along the ancient sacred way from Athens to Eleusis.

properties.name: Araphen
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 D2 Araphen

properties.name: Artemis Tauropolos temple
properties.desc: Near Artemida/Loutsa in modern Attiki, the archaeological remains of a temple in the Doric order were first identified in 1956. Excavators identified the sanctuary as belonging to Artemis Tauropolos. The compilers of the Barrington Atlas…

properties.name: Brauron/sanctuary of Artemis Brauronia
properties.desc: Brauron was a sacred site in Attica dedicated to Artemis Brauronia. The sanctuary was active from the Middle Bronze Age period, although a gap in activity stretches from the Final Bronze Age to the eighth century B.C.

properties.name: Atene
properties.desc: Atene was a paralia (coastal) deme of Attica and belonged to the phyle Antiochis.

properties.name: Temple of Athena at Sounion
properties.desc: The Temple of Athena at Sounion (ca. 470 B.C.) with its L-shaped colonnade was built on the site of an earlier temple (sixth century B.C.) at the same location.

properties.name: Temple of Athena Skiras on Salamis
properties.desc: This sanctuary, reported by Herodotus, is thought to have been located on the modern Cape Arapis in the northeast part of the island of Salamis, just north of the modern naval base. It is not to be confused with the Temple of Athena Skiras…

properties.name: Athmonon
properties.desc: Athmonon was an ancient inland deme of the tribe Kekropis in Attica, north-east of the city of Athens at modern Marousi, best known as location of a sanctuary and festival of Artemis Amarysia.

properties.name: Aulis
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B1 Aulis

properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B2 Azenia?

properties.desc: Boutadai was a deme of Attica.

properties.name: Cholargos

properties.name: Daidalidai
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B3 Daidalidai

properties.name: Deiradiotai?
properties.desc: Deiradiotai?, an Attic deme of the tribe Leontis.

properties.name: Dekeleia
properties.desc: Dekeleia was an inland deme of the tribe Hippothontis, in Attica, located 120 stades from Athens. In myth, Dekeleia ceded its autonomy under Theseus to form the city-state of Athens.

properties.name: Dema
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B2 Dema

properties.name: Diomeia
properties.desc: Diomeia was a deme of Attica, and it was located both within and outside the walls of Themistocles at Athens. The deme was named after the hero Diomos, a son of Kollytos.

properties.name: Eiresidai
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B3 Eiresidai

properties.name: Eitea (Antiochis)
properties.desc: Eitea was an Attic deme of the tribe Antiochis, probably located at the site of modern-day Grammatiko.

properties.name: Elaious?
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B2 Elaious?

properties.name: Eleusis
properties.desc: Eleusis, located some 22 km west of Athens, was the site of the cult of Demeter and the sanctuary where the Eleusinian Mysteries were celebrated from the Bronze Age to the Roman Imperial period. It was a coastal deme of the Hippothontis…

properties.name: Epikephisia
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B2 Epikephisia

properties.name: Erchia
properties.desc: Erchia was an inland deme of the tribe Aigeis in Attica.

properties.name: Erikeia?
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B2 Erikeia?

properties.name: Eroiadai
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B2 Eroiadai

properties.name: Euonymon
properties.desc: A classical deme of Attica, located at modern Trachones / Ano Kalamaki. The area has been continuously exploited or inhabited by humans since at least the Neolithic period.

properties.name: Eupyridai
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B2 Eupyridai

properties.name: Gargettos
properties.desc: Gargettos was an inland deme of the tribe Aigeis in Attica, probably located south of Mt Pentalikon in the area of modern Gerakas.

properties.name: Hagnous
properties.desc: Hagnous was a deme of Attica adjacent to the demoi Pallene and Gargettus.

properties.name: Halai Aixonides
properties.desc: Halai Aixonides was an Attic paralia deme of the Kekropis phyle. It was located near Cape Zoster on the western coast of Attica, south of the deme Aixones, from which the second part of its name derives.

properties.name: Halai Araphenides
properties.desc: A coastal deme of the tribe Aigeis, in Attica, located on the eastern shore north of Brauron. The site was known in antiquity for its sanctuary dedicated to Artemis Tauropolos.

properties.name: Halimous
properties.desc: Halimous was a city deme of the tribe Leontis, south of Athens at Cape Kolias, perhaps on the modern Hagia Anna hill.

properties.name: Hekale?
properties.desc: Hekale was a deme of ancient Attica, likely situated in the plain of Marathon. It derived its name from Hecale, an old woman who aided Theseus in his hunt for the Marathonian bull and whom the hero subsequently honored.

properties.name: Heleon
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 A1 Heleon

properties.name: Hermos

properties.name: Hestiaia?

properties.name: Kephale

properties.name: Kephisia

properties.name: Kerameis

properties.name: Koile
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B3 Koile

properties.name: Kolonai
properties.desc: An Attic deme, located on Mount Pentelicon near Hecale or Michaleza.

properties.name: Kolonos
properties.desc: Kolonos was a deme assigned to the phyle Aegeis in Attica. It was located to the north of the Academy and provided the setting for one of the tragedies of Sophocles. The district is associated with the god Poseidon.

properties.name: Konthyle

properties.name: Kytherros

properties.name: Lakiadai

properties.desc: A deme located to the east of Mt. Hymettus. The site is located on the eastern outskirts of modern Liopesi. The epithet "Lower" ("Hypenerthen") distinguished it from the small Upper Paiania, but the two formed a single entity for many…

properties.name: Paiania Kathyperthen
properties.desc: Paiania was an inland deme of the tribe Pandionis, in Attica. The epithet "Kathyperthen" (Upper) distinguished it from nearby Lower Paiania, but the two formed a single entity for many purposes.

properties.name: Paionidai

properties.name: Palaiokoundoura

properties.name: Pallene
properties.desc: Pallene was an ancient mesogeia deme of the phyle Antiochis in Attica, located at Stavros in what is now the Gerakas suburb of Athens.

properties.name: Cave of Pan and the Nymphs
properties.desc: A small cave, located northeast of Vari in Attica, Greece, that was used as a shrine dedicated to Apollo, Pan, and the Nymphs from the sixth to the second centuries BC.

properties.name: Peiraieus/Piraeus
properties.desc: The ancient, fortified port settlement of ancient Athens. It was also the coastal deme of the tribe Hippothoontis.

properties.desc: Prasia or Prasiai was a coastal deme of the tribe Pandionis, located in Attica, on the Koroni peninsula.

properties.name: Probalinthos
properties.desc: An ancient deme of Athens in the plain of Marathon.

properties.name: Prospalta
properties.desc: Prospalta was an Attic deme of the phyle Acamantis. Its location was in the interior, between Zoster and Potamus.

properties.name: Rhamnous
properties.desc: Rhamnous was an ancient settlement of Attica adjacent to the Euboean Strait and a coastal deme of the tribe Aiantis.

properties.name: Salamis (settlement)
properties.desc: The ancient city of Salamis was located on the Saronic island of the same name, overlooking the modern Ampelaki Bay to the east. The site was likely largely in the area now covered by the modern city of Ambelaki/Ampelaki.

properties.name: Semachidai?
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 C2 Semachidai?

properties.name: Sphettos
properties.desc: Sphettos was an inland deme of Akamantis, in Attica, near modern Koropi.

properties.name: Steiria
properties.desc: Steiria was a deme of ancient Attica. It was located on the east coast of Attica, between Prasiae and Brauron, and belonged to the phyle of Pandionis.

properties.name: Sypalettos

properties.name: Tanagra

properties.name: Teithras

properties.desc: Thymaitadai was a city deme of the tribe Hippothoontis in Attica, located in modern Keratsini, a western suburb of Piraeus.

properties.name: Porta Eburnea
properties.desc: The so-called Porta Eburnea or the Arco della Mandorla is an ancient gate of the Etruscan walls of Perusia.

properties.name: Worthy Down
properties.desc: A Middle Iron Age-3rd/4th century A.D. settlement complex at Worthy Down, lying 8 km. NNW of Winchester.

properties.name: Villa Romana Baláca
properties.desc: The site of a Roman villa that was discovered in 1904 in the Balácapuszta field of Vámos village in western Hungary.

properties.name: Theater at Leuke
properties.desc: The theater is located at the north-east end of Kouphonesi. It was a stone-built building that could accommodated ca. 1000 spectators.

properties.name: Roman Baths of Como
properties.desc: The Roman Baths of Como were in use from the later first century until the third century CE.

properties.name: Roman baths, Spoleto
properties.desc: Roman baths located at Spoletium.

properties.name: South-Western Baths
properties.desc: A bath complex at Herculaneum that was discovered in the excavations of the so-called "Insula Occidentalis". It was not in use as a bath at the time of the 79 CE eruption as it had been repurposed as a ship-shed.

properties.name: Theater of Chersonesos
properties.desc: A Hellenistic theater located in the ancient Greek colony of Tauric Chersonesos. Built in the 4th or 3rd century BC, it remained in use through the Roman period. It is one of the few surviving examples of Greek theater architecture in the…

properties.name: Boviolles
properties.desc: Gallo-Roman hilltop settlement

properties.name: Library of Pantainos
properties.desc: The modern name for a library built on the southeast corner of the Agora in Athens by Flavius Pantainos ca. 97-102 AD. It was demolished to make way for the Post-Herulian Wall in the late third century AD.

properties.name: Esparragalejo dam
properties.desc: Dating to the first century AD, the Esparragalejo dam is the earliest known multiple arch buttress dam.

properties.name: Tomb of Lucius Sepunius Sandilianus
properties.desc: The Tomb of Lucius Sepunius Sandilianus is a Roman-period tomb, possibly of tholos typology, located in the Porta Nocera necropolis of Pompeii.

properties.name: Kydathenaion
properties.desc: Kydathenaion was the third largest deme of Attica, with only Acharnae and Aphidna being larger. It was located within the city walls of Athens and perhaps included the Acropolis and the Areopagus as well.

properties.name: Melite
properties.desc: Melite was a deme of ancient Attica. It was located in the urban center of Athens and included both the Agora and the Pnyx. It belonged to the tribe of Kekropis.

properties.name: Kollytos
properties.desc: An Attic asty deme belonging to the Aegeis phyle.

properties.name: Skambonidai
properties.desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 59 B3 Skambonidai

properties.name: Schola Praeconum
properties.desc: The so-called Schola Praeconum is located at the foot of the Palatine Hill near the church of S. Anastasia. A black-and-white floor mosaic discovered during excavations depicts public heralds known as praecones, thus the name of the site.

properties.name: Untitled

properties.name: Mine of Laureion

properties.name: Acquedotto dei Sette Bassi
properties.desc: A Roman aqueduct supplying the Villa dei Sette Bassi.

properties.name: House of Plotilla
properties.desc: The House of Plotilla, also known as Casa di Apollo e Coronide, was excavated in 1815 and again in 1839. It lies in Regio VIII of Pompeii.

properties.name: Western gate of Serdica
properties.desc: Fortification at the western edge of the settlement of Serdica, constructed in the 2nd century CE and disused by the end of the 6th century CE. The site was excavated in 2011-2013 and is now an archaeological park.

properties.name: Tre Ponti necropolis
properties.desc: A necropolis along the Via Amerina, likely in use from the third century BC until the third century AD.

properties.name: Sant'Ilario
properties.desc: A paleochristian site located at the thirtieth mile of the ancient via Labicana, near to the ancient road station 'ad Bivium'.

properties.name: Colombarone
properties.desc: An archaeological site that preserves remains of a Late Roman settlement along the Via Flaminia.

properties.name: Villa di Teodorico
properties.desc: A palatial Roman villa and bath complex that has been connected with Theodoric the Great, with twentieth century interpretations labeling it as Theodoric's "hunting lodge". More recent excavations have uncovered evidence for earlier…

properties.name: Villa del Vergigno, Montelupo Fiorentino
properties.desc: A large villa rustica inhabited from ca. 100 B.C. to A.D. 500, located near Montelupo Fiorentino in the mid-Arno Valley of northern Tuscany, approximately twenty km west of Florence.

properties.name: Marina di Palo Roman villa
properties.desc: An Imperial maritime villa located in Ladispoli, Italy.

properties.name: Temple of Hera, Olympia
properties.desc: The Temple of Hera at Olympia, also known as the Heraion, is a peripteral temple located in the northwest corner of the Altis precinct, dedicated to Hera. Built ca. 600-590 B.C., the Heraion is the oldest temple at Olympia and one of the…

properties.name: Dema wall
properties.desc: The so-called Dema wall was a built fortification of ancient Attica that was intended to a close a gap between between Aigaleos and Parnes. The wall's course originally ran more than 4 km.

properties.name: Roman theater of Milan
properties.desc: The Roman theater of Milan was built during the Augustan period and could accommodate 7,000 to 9,000 spectators.

properties.name: Villa Imperiale of Milan
properties.desc: A palatial Roman villa dating to the reign of Maximian.

properties.name: Roman amphitheater of Beneventum
properties.desc: The Roman amphitheater of Beneventum dates to the reign of the emperor Nero.

properties.name: Porta Napoli (Alife)
properties.desc: One of the four gates of the fortified castrum of Allifae. The fortifications are thought to date to the Late Republican period on the basis of building techniques.

properties.name: Porta Fiume (Alife)
properties.desc: One of the four gates of the fortified castrum of Allifae. The fortifications are thought to date to the Late Republican period on the basis of building techniques.

properties.name: Lantonside
properties.desc: A Roman fortlet of Antonine period in Scotland.

properties.name: Hedemünden
properties.desc: An early Imperial fort located on the river Werra.

properties.name: Mausoleum of Gallienus
properties.desc: A mausoleum on the Via Appia that has been identified conventionally as that of the emperor Gallienus.

properties.name: Mons Faliscorum

properties.name: Roman theater at Cales

properties.name: Basilica Damasiana
properties.desc: The basilica and oratory of Damasianus, as well as the martyr tombs of Simplicius, Faustinus, Beatrice, and Ruinianus.

properties.name: Trajanic harbor
properties.desc: The hexagonal Trajanic harbor basin at Portus was built between 100 and 112. Its maximum diameter is approximately 716 meters.

properties.name: Oldbury Camp
properties.desc: An Iron Age hillfort located in Kent that dates to the first century A.D. and shows signs for at least partial reorganization following the Roman invasion of Britain.

properties.name: Wickham Bushes Romano-British settlement
properties.desc: The Romano-British settlement at Wickham Bushes is located due south from Caesar's Camp. A range of archaeological material was recovered, including numismatic evidence that ranges in date from Agrippa to Valentinian II.

properties.name: Middlewich Roman fort
properties.desc: A Roman fort in use in the late first century CE near Salinae at Harbutt's Field, Middlewich.

properties.name: Ödes Schloss bridgehead fort
properties.desc: A Roman bridgehead fort, located near Carnuntum (modern Bad Deutsch-Altenburg in Austria).

properties.name: Classical Stadium at Olympia
properties.desc: As key competitive and spectator fixtures of the ancient Olympic games, stadia at the sanctuary of Olympia were relocated, renovated, and modified throughout the history of the games, which stretched from at least the archaic period to the…

properties.name: Teatro Clunia
properties.desc: A Roman theater initially constructed during the reign of Tiberius.

properties.name: East Creech villa
properties.desc: A Roman villa with mosaic floors and columns was discovered between East Creech and Cotness in 1869.

properties.name: Roman theater of Fourvière
properties.desc: A Roman theater in Lyon, France, that originally dates ca. 15 B.C.

properties.name: House of the Rhodian Peristyle at Italica
properties.desc: Roman house at Italica, also known as the House of the Rhodian Patio. Constructed on a slope, the house has a multileveled patio, with sections of different heights connected by stairs.

properties.name: Haltwhistle Burn Roman Fortlet and Camp
properties.desc: Site of Roman fortlet and temporary camp. The fortlet guarded the crossing of the Burn by the Stanegate. It pre-dates the construction of Hadrian's Wall, which passes 0.5 km to the north.

properties.name: Aquis Querquennis
properties.desc: A first-century A.D. Roman encampment along the Via Nova.

properties.name: Stoke Hill
properties.desc: The site of a possible Roman signal station.

properties.name: Cividade de Bagunte
properties.desc: The Cividade de Bagunte is a fortified Iron Age site that became Romanized. It is located in the municipality of Vila do Conde in the Porto district of Portugal.

properties.name: Whitemoss Roman auxiliary fort
properties.desc: A Roman auxiliary fort built ca. A.D. 140 that protected the western flank of the Antonine Wall.

properties.name: Kinvaston Fort
properties.desc: Kinvaston Fort, a Roman vexillation fort located near the point where the Watling Street crossed the River Penk. The fort was discovered via air photos in 1946.

properties.name: Huntingdonshire Monument 97
properties.desc: An Iron Age and early Roman farmstead located near Orton Longueville, Cambridgeshire. Salvage excavations were conducted in 1974 prior to highway construction that destroyed the site.

properties.name: Gallo-Roman Theater of Lillebonne
properties.desc: The Gallo-Roman Theater of Lillebonne was in use from the first to the third century.

properties.name: Ponte Brabaciera
properties.desc: A second-century Roman bridge on the Riu Brabaciera.

properties.name: Adro Vello
properties.desc: The remains of a Roman villa and necropolis.

properties.name: Roman furnaces in Alcamo
properties.desc: A productive site in Alcamo Marina was discovered in 2000 and includes kilns from the Roman period.

properties.name: Roman castrum at Pyrgi
properties.desc: The Roman castrum at Pyrgi seems to re-use, in a direct fashion, elements of the preceding Etruscan city plan, although covering a smaller area.

properties.name: Greek theater of Taormina
properties.desc: The Greek theater of Taormina was built originally in the third century B.C.

properties.name: Greek theater of Tyndaris
properties.desc: The Greek theater of Tyndaris dates originally to the fourth century B.C.

properties.name: Roman baths of Taormina
properties.desc: The Roman baths of Taormina are built atop a public building of the Hellenistic period. The Roman baths originally fronted on the forum and were expanded in the second century.

properties.name: Area archeologica di Casarinaccio
properties.desc: During archaeological excavations carried out between 1926 and 1934 in Casarinaccio (Ardea), a monumental complex was identified. This consisted of a late republican basilica (first century BCE) and the remains of an archaic temple…

properties.name: Roman amphitheater at Rudiae
properties.desc: The Roman amphitheater at Rudiae is part of the complement of Roman buildings dating to the imperial period.

properties.name: Roman amphitheater at Santa Maria Capua Vetere
properties.desc: Sometimes referred to as the "Anfiteatro Campano", the Roman amphitheater at Santa Maria Capua Vetere is the second largest in the Roman world. Begun under Augustus, it was further renovated under Hadrian and Antoninus Pius.

properties.name: Horncastle

properties.name: Franks Roman villa
properties.desc: The site of a Roman villa with two parallel ranges of rooms dating from the second half of the first century to the fifth century.

properties.name: Staigue stone fort
properties.desc: An Iron Age ring fort, dating perhaps to the fourth century AD.

properties.name: Sanctuaries of Apollo Deiradiotes and Athena Oxyderkes
properties.desc: At Argos, Pausanias mentions both the sanctuary of Apollo Deiradiotes (Apollo of the ridge) and the sanctuary of Athena Oxyderkes (Athena the clear-sighted).

properties.name: Hellenistic and Roman quarter archaeological area
properties.desc: The Hellenistic and Roman area is orthogonally planned and covers more than 15,000 square meters. It is located near Poggio San Nicola.

properties.name: Villa del Río Roman bridge
properties.desc: A Roman bridge along the Via Augusta.

properties.name: Villamargo
properties.desc: A Roman villa.

properties.name: Ponte Lupo
properties.desc: Remains of a portion of the Aqua Marcia aqueduct located near Gallicano nel Lazio.

properties.name: Roman baths at Oescus
properties.desc: The Roman baths at Oescus are dated to the middle of the third century.

properties.name: Porta Settimiana
properties.desc: The Porta Settimiana is a gate in Rome's Aurelianic walls.

properties.name: Grotta del Mortale
properties.desc: A Republican period cistern located along the present-day Via Polense in the Comune of Poli in Rome's eastern suburbs.

properties.name: Grotto of the Sibyl
properties.desc: A cave discovered by Amedeo Maiuri in 1932 and connected in the historical tradition with the Cumaean Sibyl. The site features in the sixth book of Virgil's Aeneid.

properties.name: Coesike West temporary camps
properties.desc: A sequence of temporary camps located south of the vallum associated with Hadrian's Wall.

properties.name: Camp du Château
properties.desc: A large oppidum active in the Late Bronze and early Iron Ages.

properties.name: The Theater of Larissa
properties.desc: The theater at Larissa was a large stone theater built around the end of the third century BC and used for dramatic performances and as a political meeting place.

properties.name: Roman Forum (Mérida)
properties.desc: The Roman Forum in Mérida, Spain, dates ca. 25 BCE. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1993.

properties.name: Temple of Concordia, Agrigento
properties.desc: The Temple of Concord, located in the so-called "Valle dei Templi" of Agrigento, dates ca. 440-430 B.C.

properties.name: Formello villa and mausoleum
properties.desc: A Roman villa in the territory of Blera of which a cistern and a mausoleum remain.

properties.name: Valdonega Roman villa
properties.desc: The Roman villa of Valdonega near Verona dates to the first century A.D.

properties.name: Forum of Suasa
properties.desc: The Forum of Suasa measures 50 x 100 meters and is surrounded by a portico.

properties.name: Basilica

properties.name: So-called Oratory of Phalaris
properties.desc: A small, rectangular Greek temple-type building dated to the first century B.C. and located in the upper agora of Agrigento, on the Poggetto di San Nicola. The name "Oratory" comes from its later use as a Christian chapel.

properties.name: Baths of Cilurnum
properties.desc: The Roman military bathhouse at Cilurnum.

properties.name: Temple of Jupiter
properties.desc: A temple dedicated to the Capitoline triad is located on the forum of Saepinum.

properties.name: Brownhart Law
properties.desc: A Roman fortlet in Scotland was previously interpreted as a signal station.

properties.name: Gatehouse-of-Fleet
properties.desc: A Roman fortlet built during Agricola's campaigns ca. 80 CE. RENames would identify it with the Camulossesa attested in the Ravenna Cosmography.

properties.name: Roman baths at Carnuntum
properties.desc: The Roman baths at Carnuntum.

properties.name: Roman amphitheater at Lucus Feroniae
properties.desc: The Roman amphitheater at Lucus Feroniae was financed by one M. Silius Epaphroditus, who in turn received the title patronus. The structure dates to the reign of Tiberius.

properties.name: Raeburnfoot
properties.desc: Raeburnfoot is a small Roman fort near the junction of the river Esk and the Rae Burn.

properties.name: Sauve Pre-Roman oppidum
properties.desc: A pre-Roman and Gallo-Roman oppidum in the territory of the Volcae Arecomici.

properties.name: Augusta Bagiennorum amphitheater
properties.desc: The Roman amphitheater of Augusta Bagiennorum.

properties.name: Roman amphitheater at Egnatia/Gnathia
properties.desc: The so-called Roman amphitheater at Egnatia/Gnathia dates to the Iulio-Claudian period. It is an elliptical structure with walls in opus Africanum that were revetted with painted plaster.

properties.name: Little Oakley Roman villa
properties.desc: The site of a Roman villa that was partially excavated in 1939 and then again from 1951 to 1978. The site was occupied from ca. A.D. 60 until the fourth century.

properties.name: Column of Marcus Aurelius
properties.desc: The Column of Marcus Aurelius is a monumental victory column erected along the Via Lata between 176 and 193 CE. The monument celebrated victories realized against the Marcomanni and the Sarmatians (172-175 CE).

properties.name: Ponte di Pietra
properties.desc: A Roman segmental stone arch bridge located near Augusta Praetoria.

properties.name: Stele of Caius Vibius Quartus

properties.name: Pagliano Roman port
properties.desc: A riverine port near the confluence of the Tiber and Paglia rivers.

properties.name: Theater of Tegea

properties.name: Mausoleo di Ummidia Quadratilla

properties.name: Cirauqui
properties.desc: Remains of a Roman bridge and paved road.

properties.name: Roman Town House, Dorchester

properties.name: Roman amphitheater at Durno(no)varia
properties.desc: The Neolithic henge known as Maumbury Rings was adapted for use as an amphitheater space during the Roman period.

properties.name: Mithraeum at Mundelsheim
properties.desc: A second-century Mithraeum is located in the area of the municipality of Mundelsheim in the Ludwigsburg district of Baden-Württemberg, Germany.

properties.name: Arènes de Lutèce
properties.desc: The Roman amphitheater of Lutetia (modern Paris).

properties.name: Andernos-les-Bains
properties.desc: A Gallo-Roman villa.

properties.name: Roman theater at Volaterrae
properties.desc: The Roman theater of Volaterrae was built during the during the Augustan period under the consulship of Aulus Caecina Severus.

properties.name: Theater at Stymphalos

properties.name: Roman amphitheater at Carsulae
properties.desc: The Roman amphitheater at Carsulae dates to the first century A.D.
